Techniques Used: Iterative Algorithm for Switching Cost Optimization
Influence Modeling (Cascading and Linear Threshold Models)
Application Areas: Disaster Response and Search and Rescue
Supply Chain and Transportation Network Robustness
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Stochastic Resource Optimization: Formulating dynamic scheduling problems under uncertainty using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and iterative algorithms to maximize expected utility (e.g., lives saved) while minimizing switching costs for drone fleets in disaster scenarios.

Causal Failure Propagation Analysis: Modeling directed flow networks to identify and mitigate cascading link failures by formulating discrete optimization problems (MILP) that determine maximum sustainable causal failures while maintaining flow demand.

Interdependent Layer Interdiction: Developing Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) models to interdict weaponized disinformation in social networks, linearizing competitive information diffusion to protect physical infrastructure layers like subway systems from demand-induced disruptions.

Adversarial Behavior Simulation: Integrating epidemiological models (SIR) and linear threshold models with network science to simulate how adversarial manipulation of human behavior affects traffic routing and power grid stability, informing robustness strategies for critical infrastructure.
Summary Description: Sridhar Radhakrishnan specializes in System of Systems Engineering, focusing on the resilience and optimization of critical infrastructure and autonomous systems. His research bridges operations research, network science, and cybersecurity to address complex challenges in disaster management, supply chain security, and cyber-physical threats. He employs advanced mathematical modeling, including Integer Linear Programming (ILP), Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), and stochastic utility modeling, to solve NP-hard problems in drone scheduling and network flow optimization. A key contribution is his work on interdependent layers, specifically analyzing how weaponized disinformation in social networks can disrupt physical infrastructure like power grids and transportation systems. By integrating behavioral models with network robustness analysis, he develops mitigation strategies for cascading failures and adversarial attacks, enhancing the reliability of urban and national security systems.
